description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt to use an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) to inject/override authorization parameters at the auth endpoint.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or process an unsigned request object (alg=none) such that attacker-controlled parameters are consumed without authenticity verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none) and processed it, indicating proof integrity failure for request object signature verification.

description: Brokered-flow attack: token exchange with a control (valid subject_token) followed by an attack (tampered/untrusted subject_token) to detect signature/issuer trust bypass.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex token exchange must verify the exact upstream proof (subject_token) against the configured OIDC connector trust anchor; tampered/untrusted tokens must be rejected while a valid control exchange succeeds.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_control_exchange_http_status < 400 AND user_control_exchange_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-flow failures to proof verification (setup or connector misconfiguration likely).
Dex accepted a tampered/unverifiable subject_token during token exchange, indicating proof integrity failure (signature/issuer/audience not enforced on consumed proof).

description: Brokered-flow + config change: enable an OIDC connector with insecure_skip_signature_validation=true and attempt to authenticate; secure behavior is to reject or not allow such a connector to be used to accept unsigned/untrusted proofs.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Even if a connector is (mis)configured to skip signature validation, Dex should not accept unauthenticated upstream proofs as valid identities; otherwise Verify(proof) is not applied to the consumed proof semantics.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authentication succeeded under a connector configured to skip signature validation, suggesting Dex consumed an unauthenticated proof as an authenticated identity (proof integrity failure).

description: Direct endpoint: attempt unsigned request object (alg=none) to override authorization parameters (redirect_uri/scope) and see if Dex processes attacker-controlled semantics without signature verification.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or process an unsigned (alg=none) OIDC request object such that consumed authorization parameters differ from what would be verified under a signed request-object policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, attacker-controlled authorization parameters may be consumed without authenticity verification.

description: Brokered-flow: token exchange with a control (valid subject_token) then an attack token intended to simulate kid-injection/untrusted-key signing; Dex must reject the untrusted subject_token under the connector trust policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the exact upstream token proof (signature/key/issuer) it consumes during token exchange; an attacker-signed token (e.g., via kid injection pointing to attacker key) must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-flow results to proof-integrity enforcement (likely setup/grant/connector issue).
Dex accepted an attacker-controlled/untrusted subject_token (kid-injection/untrusted-key style), indicating proof verification may not match consumed semantics.

description: Direct endpoint: attempt unsigned request object (alg=none) to smuggle/override authorization parameters (scope/redirect_uri) and see if Dex accepts and processes it without signature verification.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume attacker-controlled authorization semantics from an unsigned request object; if it accepts alg=none and processes embedded params, Verify(proof) != Consume(proof).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; attacker-controlled authorization semantics may be consumed without authenticity verification.
Control request-object probe failed unexpectedly; results may be inconclusive due to endpoint/config mismatch rather than proof-integrity enforcement.

description: Brokered-flow: token exchange control with a plausible subject_token, then an attack exchange using a subject_token that simulates kid/header injection (untrusted key selection). Dex must reject the attack token under connector trust policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the exact JWT it consumes during token exchange; attacker-controlled header fields (e.g., kid) must not cause acceptance of an untrusted signature/key.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack failure/success to proof-integrity enforcement.
Dex accepted a subject_token that simulates kid/header injection to an attacker-controlled key; signature verification may not be applied to the consumed proof.

description: Direct endpoint I1: attempt to smuggle attacker-controlled authorization parameters via an unsigned request object (alg=none) while also providing conflicting safe query params; server must not accept/act on unsigned request object semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume authorization parameters from an unsigned request object (alg=none); if it does, it may verify one semantic proof (query params) but consume a different one (request object), violating proof integrity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object at the authorization endpoint, indicating it may consume attacker-controlled authorization semantics without authenticity verification (proof integrity violation).

description: Authorization-code replay: redeem the same authorization code twice and ensure the second redemption is rejected (one-time artifact). Includes a control successful redemption first.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be accepted more than once; the second exchange must fail even if all parameters match.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (second redemption succeeded) — replay protection for one-time codes is broken.
Control failed: initial code redemption did not succeed, so replay result is inconclusive (likely client/redirect/connector misconfiguration).

description: Refresh-token replay/rotation check using token exchange: obtain a refresh token, then attempt to reuse the same refresh token again after a successful refresh (old token should be rejected under rotation). Includes two identities to ensure no cross-session confusion.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Refresh tokens should not be reusable beyond their intended single-use window when rotation is enabled; reusing an old refresh token after it has been rotated must fail.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: refresh did not succeed, so old-refresh-token reuse test is inconclusive.
Old refresh token was accepted after rotation (replay succeeded) — refresh token anti-replay/rotation enforcement is broken.

description: Token exchange freshness: perform a control token exchange with a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with an expired subject_token (exp in the past). Uses two identities and includes the required control flow.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject expired upstream subject tokens; a subject_token with exp in the past must not be accepted even if signature/issuer are otherwise valid.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: valid subject_token exchange did not succeed; expired-token result is inconclusive (could be connector/grant/basic-auth setup).
Dex accepted an expired subject_token during token exchange — freshness enforcement on exp is broken.

description: Refresh-token replay after explicit revocation: obtain refresh_token, revoke it, then attempt token_exchange using the revoked refresh_token as subject_token (should be rejected). Includes a control exchange before revocation.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A revoked credential artifact (refresh_token) must not be accepted for token exchange after revocation; revocation should make the artifact unusable immediately.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute post-revocation behavior to freshness/revocation enforcement.
Revoked refresh_token was still accepted for token exchange (replay after revocation).

description: Access-token replay after revocation: obtain a session_token (access token) via password grant, revoke it, then attempt to use it to call userinfo (verify_granted_identity) and also as subject_token in token_exchange. Includes a second identity as control.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After revocation, an access token must not be usable for protected calls (userinfo) nor as a subject_token for token exchange.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Revoked access token still succeeded on userinfo (token remained usable after revocation).
Revoked access token was accepted as subject_token for token exchange (replay after revocation).

description: I2 replay: obtain an access token via password grant, revoke it, then attempt to keep using it (userinfo) and also exchange it again via token_exchange; both should be rejected after revocation. Includes a second identity as a control for baseline userinfo success.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoked session/access tokens must not remain usable for userinfo or as subject_token in token exchange after revocation.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Revoked access token remained usable for /userinfo (token should not be accepted after revocation).
Revoked access token was accepted as subject_token in token exchange (replay after revocation).
Control userinfo failed; cannot attribute failures to revocation/freshness enforcement.

description: I2 replay: obtain a refresh_token via password grant (offline_access), then attempt to use the same refresh_token twice as a subject_token in token_exchange. If Dex enforces one-time/rotation semantics for refresh tokens, the second exchange should be rejected. Includes a second identity to ensure baseline exchange works.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Refresh tokens should not be reusable beyond their intended one-time/rotation semantics; repeated use should be rejected (or at least not continuously accepted).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Same refresh_token was accepted multiple times in token exchange (replay/rotation not enforced).
Control refresh-token exchange failed; cannot attribute replay result to freshness enforcement.

description: I2 replay: obtain an id_token via password grant, revoke the session, then attempt to use the revoked id_token as a subject_token in token_exchange. Also verify that the original session can no longer call userinfo. Includes a second identity to ensure token exchange works in general.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoked ID tokens (or the session they are bound to) must not remain usable for token exchange; revocation should prevent further acceptance.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Revoked session remained usable for /userinfo (revocation not enforced).
Revoked ID token was accepted in token exchange (replay after revocation).
Control ID-token exchange failed; cannot attribute failures to freshness enforcement.

description: Authorization-code flow: redeem a valid auth code once (control), then attempt to redeem the same code again after a simulated delay to detect missing one-time use / TTL enforcement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts and must not be accepted more than once, including after their intended lifetime (TTL).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial authorization_code exchange did not succeed; cannot attribute replay outcome to freshness/anti-replay enforcement.
Control failed: second identity could not complete code exchange; environment/client/connector may be misconfigured.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay) — one-time artifact freshness/anti-replay violated.

description: I3: Attempt to redeem an authorization code without any client authentication (no client_secret) and without PKCE verifier, to detect step-skipping / missing client binding at the token endpoint.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct client authentication context; exchanging a code without client auth (and without PKCE) must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control code exchange failed; cannot attribute attack failure/success to flow-coherence enforcement.
Authorization code was redeemed without client authentication (and without PKCE verifier) — token endpoint accepted a step-skipped / unbound redemption.

description: I3: Attempt to redeem an authorization code using a different redirect_uri than used at authorization time, to detect cross-flow splicing.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the original redirect_uri; mismatched redirect_uri at /token must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted authorization code with mismatched redirect_uri — indicates cross-flow splicing / broken redirect binding.
Control exchanges failed; cannot distinguish redirect binding enforcement from general OIDC misconfiguration.

description: I3: Cross-session splicing attempt: use an auth code from session A in session B (code injection) while preserving each session's original state values.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code must be bound to the initiating browser session/state; a code from session A must not be redeemable in session B context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Session B successfully redeemed Session A's authorization code (cross-session splicing / code injection) — flow coherence violated.
Control exchanges failed; cannot attribute injection outcome to session binding enforcement.

description: OIDC code flow state-swap attempt across two browser sessions: start two auth requests with distinct state values, then attempt to complete session B using session A's state (should be rejected / not yield a valid token).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization response must be bound to the initiating browser session via the original state value; swapping state across sessions must not allow code redemption.

oracle_checks.violation_description: State-swap/callback splicing succeeded: token endpoint accepted an auth code in a mismatched state/session context.
State-swap/callback splicing yielded a usable session (userinfo succeeded) when it should not.

description: PKCE step-skipping attempt: initiate an auth request that uses PKCE (code_challenge out-of-band), then redeem the code without code_verifier. Expected secure behavior: reject redemption (hardening check for flow coherence).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: When an authorization request used PKCE, the token exchange must be bound to the original PKCE verifier; skipping code_verifier must not succeed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: PKCE step skipping succeeded: code redeemed without code_verifier even though the auth request used PKCE.
PKCE step skipping produced a usable session (userinfo succeeded) when it should not.

description: Request object parameter confusion: send an unsigned request object (alg=none) that attempts to override redirect_uri/state while also providing outer query params. If Dex processes the unsigned request object, it could desynchronize the flow and allow step-splicing.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization request parameters must be coherent and bound to the initiating session; unsigned request objects must not be accepted to override critical parameters (redirect_uri/state) and cause flow desynchronization.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted, enabling parameter override and potential flow desynchronization/splicing.
Flow completed successfully after unsigned request-object parameter override attempt; indicates possible request-parameter confusion and broken flow coherence.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_reqobj_attacker_exchange_http_status >= 400 OR user_reqobj_attacker_exchange_http_status is None OR user_reqobj_attacker_exchange_http_status == 0
oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request-object override attempt resulted in a usable session (token exchange succeeded unexpectedly).

description: I3 step-skipping in token exchange: perform a control token_exchange with connector_id, then attempt token_exchange omitting connector_id to see if Dex incorrectly accepts an unbound exchange.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to an explicit upstream connector/session context; omitting connector_id must not succeed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot interpret omission test as flow-coherence enforcement.
Token exchange succeeded without connector_id, suggesting step-skipping/unbound exchange that could enable cross-connector/session splicing.

description: I3 cross-session splicing via token exchange: attacker authenticates as self but submits victim's subject_token in token_exchange; Dex must not mint a token that maps to victim under attacker session context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be coherent with the authenticated session/principal; a session for attacker must not be able to exchange a victim's subject_token and obtain victim identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Test precondition failed: victim and attacker identities are not distinct, so splicing cannot be evaluated.
Attacker session successfully exchanged victim subject_token and obtained a token mapping to victim identity, indicating cross-session/principal splicing in the flow.

description: Case confusion in username: login as 'admin' vs 'Admin' via password grant and ensure Dex does not collapse them into the same downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream principals that differ only by case must not map to the same downstream subject/identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant principals collapsed into identical downstream attributes (preferred_username/email), suggesting normalization-based identity merge

description: Attempt principal collapse by sending an unsigned request object (alg=none) that sets an empty/blank login_hint while outer query uses a different login_hint; verify resulting identities remain distinct across two logins.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex processes attacker-controlled unsigned request objects, it must not normalize/blank the principal such that distinct principals map to the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Unsigned request object (alg=none) appears accepted and resulted in principal collapse (distinct principals mapped to same identity)

description: I4 empty/blank principal collision attempt: login with username='' vs username=' ' (space) via password grant and check whether Dex collapses them into the same downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (empty string vs single-space username) must not map to the same downstream subject/identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty/blank principal was accepted and collapsed into the same downstream identity as a space-only principal

description: I4 cross-protocol identity merge attempt: obtain identity via password grant for user_A, then run an OIDC auth code flow for a different principal and ensure the resulting identity does not map to user_A (no unintended merge across flows).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A principal authenticated via password grant must not be merged/collapsed with a different principal authenticated via OIDC authorization-code flow.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_C_oidc_http_status >= 400 OR (user_C_oidc_entity_id != user_A_entity_id AND user_C_oidc_entity_id != user_B_entity_id)
oracle_checks.violation_description: OIDC-authenticated principal was merged/collapsed into an existing password principal identity

description: Attempt principal confusion by using an unsigned request object (alg=none) to override login_hint: outer query uses login_hint=userA, request object uses login_hint=userB; verify resulting identities remain distinct and do not collapse.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex accepts request objects, it must not allow attacker-controlled parameter precedence to collapse or mis-bind principals (e.g., treating two distinct upstream principals as the same downstream subject).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Unsigned request object parameter precedence caused two distinct principals to collapse into the same downstream identity

description: Token-exchange scope escalation: obtain a baseline token with minimal scopes, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange requesting expanded scopes (groups/profile/federated:id). Exchanged identity/claims should not exceed upstream intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Exchanged token must not grant claims/permissions beyond the original upstream authorization intent (requested scopes) and broker policy; expanded scopes during token exchange should be rejected or not reflected in resulting claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted expanded scopes and returned group claims beyond the original upstream intent (openid email).
Control flow failed; cannot attribute token-exchange behavior to authorization binding enforcement.

description: Request object parameter override: attempt to smuggle expanded scopes via an unsigned request object (alg=none) while outer query requests minimal scope; if accepted and processed, could over-grant claims/permissions.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization request parameters (especially scope) must not be attacker-overridable via an unsigned request object; effective permissions must not exceed the intended outer request and broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object was accepted/processed and resulted in over-granted claims (e.g., groups) beyond the outer requested scope.
Control flow failed; cannot attribute request-object behavior to authorization binding.

description: Attempt to use victim's subject_token in token_exchange while authenticating as attacker client context; ensure exchanged identity remains bound to upstream intent (victim) and does not grant attacker identity/permissions.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow a client/session to obtain effective permissions for a different principal than the upstream subject_token represents (no principal/permission confusion across sessions).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted victim subject_token but rebound effective identity/permissions to attacker (or otherwise produced a third identity), violating authorization binding to upstream intent.

description: Control: normal auth request with minimal scopes. Attack: unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to expand scopes to groups/profile/federated:id; ensure Dex rejects or does not over-grant claims beyond outer requested scope.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization request parameters (especially scope) must be bound to authenticated upstream intent and broker policy; unsigned request objects must not be processed to expand effective permissions/claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted/processed and resulted in groups claim being granted despite outer scope lacking 'groups' (scope smuggling / over-grant).

description: Attempt token exchange while omitting/blanking client_secret in body to see if Dex accepts exchange without proper client authentication (authorization binding to client context). Includes a control exchange with correct client_secret.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must be bound to the authenticated client; exchanging a subject_token without valid client authentication must be rejected and must not yield a usable session_token.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_control_exchange_ok_http_status < 400 AND user_control_exchange_ok_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to authorization binding enforcement.
Dex accepted token exchange without valid client authentication, breaking authorization binding to client context.

description: Attempt to use password grant to request expanded scopes (groups/profile/federated:id) and verify Dex does not over-grant claims/permissions beyond what the password flow should allow. Includes two identities to detect cross-user over-grant/caching.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Password-grant tokens must not include claims/permissions beyond the requested and broker-allowed scope set; expanded scopes should be rejected or not reflected in granted identity claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Password grant with minimal scopes unexpectedly returned groups claim, indicating over-grant beyond requested upstream intent.
Password grant accepted expanded scopes and returned groups claim, indicating potential scope/claim over-grant beyond broker policy or upstream intent.
Two distinct password-grant logins mapped to the same downstream identity, risking cross-user permission leakage.
